tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent with explicit trigger phrases like 'why is my GuardDuty bill so high', and covers scope (protection plans, cost drivers, free trial). It is a single dense paragraph, slightly long but within acceptable range for a specialized cost-optimization skill covering multiple trigger scenarios.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when a user asks to reduce, review, audit, or optimize GuardDuty spend, or reports an unexpected GuardDuty cost increase or an expensive protection plan. Activate on requests like \"why is my GuardDuty bill so high\", \"reduce GuardDuty costs\"..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is concise and focuses on domain-specific facts (billing model, offsets, workflow) rather than explaining general concepts the agent already knows. Detailed reference data is offloaded to references/ files.
tests.evidence: GuardDuty is pay-as-you-go, per protection plan, priced on the volume of data each plan analyzes... Runtime Monitoring offsets VPC Flow Log charges

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed lookup tables, API call lists, and full opportunity check definitions are all offloaded to references/ files and only summarized briefly in the body; no large blocks of reference data or lengthy conditional branches are embedded inline.
tests.evidence: For the full per-plan metric/unit/pricing table... load references/billing-model.md when identifying which plan drives a charge

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three reference files are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies the condition/context under which to load it.
tests.evidence: load references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md). If neither Cost Explorer nor usage metrics are available...

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root in the correct format.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/critical operations (read-only API boundary, validation checks) are given exact prescriptive language, while analysis and framing tasks (e.g., ranking, tradeoff judgments) leave room for agent reasoning.
tests.evidence: It never calls CreateDetector, UpdateDetector, DeleteDetector, DisableOrganizationAdminAccount, or any protection-plan mutation.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill prefers Cost Explorer as the dollar signal with usage metrics as a fallback/reconciliation, establishing a clear default rather than listing tools as equal options.
tests.evidence: prefer Cost Explorer as the dollar signal, reconciled against the usage metrics

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (scope, inventory, collect metrics, analyze, validate, report) that applies to any GuardDuty cost review request, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Identify target scope. Ask the user which accounts and Regions to review...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a dedicated 'Known Quirks' section documenting non-obvious, environment-specific facts (e.g., Runtime Monitoring/VPC Flow Log offset, separate CloudWatch namespace for malware scans).
tests.evidence: Malware Protection for S3 lives in a separate CloudWatch namespace (AWS/GuardDuty/MalwareProtection) from the other plans (AWS/GuardDuty).

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a report and provides an output template in assets/report-template.md referenced from the body.
tests.evidence: Produce a shareable Markdown report artifact following the structure, section order, and table schemas in [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md).

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large output template is embedded inline; the only inline table is a short severity definitions table (5 rows), well under 20 lines, and the full report template is stored in assets/.
tests.evidence:

|----------|------------|-----|
| CRITICAL | Runaway cost causing large ongoing overspend | Fix within 24–48 hours |

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file report-template.md is explicitly linked in the body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies when to load it (during report generation, step 6).
tests.evidence: Step 6: Generate report. Produce a shareable Markdown report artifact following the structure... in [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Load that template when generating the report.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root in correct format.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural workflow is presented as a checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' format as required, and no separate detailed sections diverge from this numbering.
tests.evidence: - [ ] **Step 1: Identify target scope.** ... - [ ] **Step 2: Inventory detectors and protection plans.**

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: Step 5 explicitly instructs the agent to self-validate its findings (checking sums, conversions, framing, and mutation-free operation) before generating the report.
tests.evidence: Step 5: Validate findings. Before writing the report, self-check the findings: confirm estimated savings sum correctly and each traces to a cited metric or cost signal...
